cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: The Approved Explanation
cards.instruction: Protect someone or the group by maintaining a simplified account that everyone can safely repeat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. Tell the children the trip's postponed for bus repairs. They'll worry about Mr Patel.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's fine. His parked bus rolled into the pond.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. Then everyone says, 'Mr Patel is fine; the bus needs repairs.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The parents will ask whether he was driving.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then 'The parked bus needs repairs; Mr Patel is fine.' Same sentence for the office. We don't need three versions of his afternoon.

mechanism: A corrects its former school-communications pupil alarming detail into a shared repeatable account that protects the driver while preserving the relevant parked-bus fact.
confusable: Not erasing every inconvenient fact or hiding A guilt: A stabilizes a simpler accurate account across children, parents and office.
comparison: Driver reassurance for a school trip versus protecting a relative birthday speech.
